slides.title: Introduction to Pricing
slides.text:
Introduction to Pricing
Dr. Mansi Khetarpal
Assistant Professor
LM Thapar School of Management
TIET

Price is the amount of money charged for a product or a service
Price is the only element in the marketing mix that produces revenue; all other elements represent costs.
Price is also one of the most flexible marketing mix elements. Unlike product features and channel commitments, prices can be changed quickly.
Captures Value

slides.title: 1. Defining the Pricing Objective
slides.text:
1. Defining the Pricing Objective
Common pricing objectives:
Short-term profit- a price that will maximize current profits
Market penetration- to maximize market share
in price-sensitive market
Market skimming- to ‘skim the cream’ off the market
sufficient number of buyers
Quality leadership- charge relatively high price

slides.title: Cost-Based Pricing
slides.text:
Cost-Based Pricing
Markup pricing
The marketer estimates the total cost of producing or manufacturing a product and then adds a mark up or the margin that the firm wants
Mark up Price= Cost per unit + (Mark up percentage * cost per unit)

bullets.text: The marketer estimates the total cost of producing or manufacturing a product and then adds a mark up or the margin that the firm wants
Mark up Price= Cost per unit + (Mark up percentage * cost per unit)

slides.text:
If the fixed costs for making 10,000 shirts is ‘1,50,000’ and the variable cost per shirt is ’30’. Now the firm expects 30% mark up on cost.
What will the mark up price be?
Ensures that all costs are recovered and the firm makes a profit
It does not consider customer’s value perception and also the competitor’s reaction

slides.title: Target-return pricing
slides.text:
Target-return pricing
Price that yields its target rate of return on investment
Setting prices to achieve a specific return on investment (ROI) or return on sales (ROS).

bullets.text: Price that yields its target rate of return on investment
Setting prices to achieve a specific return on investment (ROI) or return on sales (ROS).

slides.title: Target-return pricing
slides.text:
Target-return pricing
Investment = ₹10 lakh Desired return = 20% = ₹2 lakh
Expected sales = 10,000 units
Desired return per unit:
₹2,00,000 ÷ 10,000 = ₹20
If unit cost = ₹100:
Target price = ₹100 + ₹20 = ₹120

slides.title: Competitive pricing
slides.text:
Competitive pricing
The firm bases its price largely on competitors’ prices
1. Going Rate or ‘Follow the Crowd’- The firm prices its products at the same level as that of the competition
This method assumes that there will be no price war within the industry. 2. Auction pricing
English (ascending)- art, collectibles
Dutch (descending)- perishable goods
3. Sealed Bid Pricing Suppliers are asked to submit their quotations as part of a
tender. The price quoted reflects the firm’s cost and its understanding of competition.

slides.title: Product Mix Pricing
slides.text:
Product Mix Pricing
Loss-leader pricing: Set the price of a specific product in such a way that maximizes the profitability of other products by stimulating the additional traffic.
2. Optional feature pricing: Main Product + Optional features/product
Restaurants (Food + Drinks)
Airline Ticket + Priority boarding

bullets.text: Loss-leader pricing: Set the price of a specific product in such a way that maximizes the profitability of other products by stimulating the additional traffic.
2. Optional feature pricing: Main Product + Optional features/product

slides.text:
3. Captive pricing: When main product requires the use of secondary product to function, this secondary product is priced high. Printer + Ink Cartridges, Razors + Blades
4. Two-part pricing: Fixed fee + variable fee
Amusement parks, Clubs
5. Product-bundling pricing: Multiple products as a bundle
